voice: An oily, wheedling stool pigeon and huckster: boastful, self-serving, and quick to flirt with 'toots,' but cowardly and evasive when cornered. Heavy contractions, 1920s slang, and malapropisms; a light touch of accent ('ain't,' 'ya,' 'gonna,' 'dunno,' dropped g's) but no phonetic respellings such as 'dat' or 'hoid.' Flirting sits between vanilla and the P2-08 rewrite. Maintainer direction, 2026-10-14; supersedes the earlier P2-08 Ziggy voice.

entries.text: I don't handle stolen goods no more, toots. And that ain't very interestin', neither.
Maybe...or maybe not. What's it worth to ya?
Then I ain't got no rumors for ya, toots.
Thanks, toots! Go on, touch me again!
How many times ya gonna ask me? I already told ya everything I know about that.
Augustini...Augustini...that name rings a bell.
Oh, yeah, ain't he the concierge over at the Plaza?
The new museum prez? Stodgy old guy, but a fine chap. Yeah, that's it, a fine chap. Good man.
I'll tell ya, most of the cops in this town stink. But O'Riley's different. He knows how to treat a mouthpiece, y'know? I made some good jack keepin' my ears open for him.
Certainly I have! One of the most up-and-up guys I know. Keeps his nose clean, but he knows how to have a good time.
Lo Fat? Nah, he ain't in my privyooliged circle of friends and requaintances.
Steve? Yeah, the dockworker, I know the guy. He ain't in my inner circle, though. Dunno much about the joe.
Hey, watch your mouth. You're talkin' to him.
Heimlich? The goon with the scars at the front door? Gave my invitation the once-over like it was a bum check. Friendly as a toll booth, that one.

Nice workin' girl. I knew her when, y'know? Now she's some big hotshot museum whaddayacallit, but back then, gentlemen paid for her company, if ya catch my drift. She's respectable now, so she'd rather I forgot.
Ernie Leach? Doesn't ring a bell.
And here I was thinkin' I knew every leech in town!
Rameses? Quiet guy, most of the time. Accountant, I think. Knows his numbers, but boy, his riddles are murder.
What makes you think I know anything about a dame like her? Sheesh, she wouldn't have nothin' to do with me. I mean, I dunno anything about her. Why ask me?
She did? What'd she say? It ain't true. Listen, that old bird couldn't keep a secret if her life depended on it, and I ain't takin' the rap for her.
Now leave me alone before I call the cops.
Or somebody.
That lady's scary. I been avoidin' her.
Tut Smith? Big fella, real serious about his old relics. With a name like that, I figured it was an alias, a pharaoh on the lam, y'know? But nah, he's the genuine article.
Never heard of the rat.
John Bow? Ain't that what they call a stiff when nobody knows his name?
Hey, that's an insult, right?
Ya mean the newspaper? Not me, sister. I get my news straight from the horse's patootie, if ya catch my drift.
Yeah, I s'pose you could say that. I'm sorta a freelance detective. I find out things the police can't, then I pass the information along. For a price.
Oh, yeah. They couldn't do their jobs without me. Swell guys, the cops. Keep me flush. Salts of the earth.
Laundry...laundry...ohhh, ya mean like washin' your clothes. Nope, I do that myself.
Not me, lady. Mostly your unsavory types hang around down there.
Look, nothin' in this joint is what it looks like. Same goes for all these mucky-mucks. Appearances can be deceivin'. Me, do I look like the brother of a famous Broadway producer? No, but I am!

Well, y'know, some days it's a rich smeltin' pot, and some days it's a big cesspool. Either way, ya gotta rise to the top, like scum, and keep your feet and your nose clean. That's how I do it, anyway.
You seen it. I saw ya in there before. It is what it is. Hey, I'm a philosopher!
Don't need no notebook. I already know everything.
Reportin' is somethin' I never had no interest in, though I coulda been a journalist if I'd wanted. Besides, I got a natural respect for confidential sources.
I could get ya one real cheap, if you're interested.
Fine! Geez! Can't blame a guy for askin'. Ya don't hafta bite my head off.
I like 'em. Keys open things, y'know? Lotsa possibilities.
'Cause there ain't no icebox upstairs? Look, lady, these appeteasers are the bunk, and there's some pretty hungry joes around here. I wouldn't be wavin' no steaks around if I was you.
Why would I know anything about that? Ya must have me confused with somebody else.
I got the constitutional of an ox. Never needed smellin' salts. Wouldn't work on me anyways; my schnoz been broke a few times.
I had an uncle used to sell the stuff. Me, I always figured it was bunk.
Sorry, lanterns is outta my field of expertises.
I don't know about no stinkin' cheese.
Hey, if I knew who THAT belonged to, would I be standin' here jawin' with ya? No sir, not me!
What do I look like? An archeometrist?
Yeah, sure! Snake lassoes! Yippie-ki-yay, little boa constrictor!
Well, Mademoiselle, ankhs is like anxiety or nervousness. Like, "I'm feelin' a lotta ankhs about goin' back in the slammer." See?
Think nothin' of it.
Oh, no, you ain't stickin' that one on ME. I never saw that thing before in my life.
My peepers ain't never needed one.
They seem to work good for lightin' porpoises.
Watney Little's file? I dunno nothin' about it. Nothin' at all. Don't ask me.
Geez, don't ask me, lady. I ain't touched a drop of THAT stuff in years.
Glad ya asked. Put your dough on Mudlark in the third at Belmont. He's a mudder.
Hey, what do I look like, a doctor? All I know is, I keep away from 'em.
Superb, simply superb. First I make a sawbuck on Tunney in Philly, and now here I am rubbin' elbow grease with the hoity-toity. Thanks for askin'!
I know the dagger was heisted. I might even know whodunit, but I ain't talkin'.
All I got's a suspicion. Nothin' solid. Besides, what've the cops done for ME lately?
I'm tryin' to protect ME! Now flit.
We talked about that before, remember? I told ya that crazy riddle Rameses passed along.
That diary could be worth somethin' in the right hands. Personal papers can be awful incriminatin'. I'd hang onto it if I was you, but that's all I'm sayin'.
Nothin' but what that egghead Najeer tells me. He's heavy into the Egypt stuff. Did I tell ya that riddle he gave me?
It was somethin' like, "What is the room you leave without entering?" and then, "What is the room you enter without leaving?"
Now, that's supposed to be some great Egyptian brain-teaser, but personally, I prefer the one about the travelin' salesman and the farmer's daughter. Heard that one?
Hey, hey, hey, little lady! I was at the party the whole time, so don't go makin' any accusertory remarks. I didn't even know the guy. Now buzz off!
Sure, the snazzy dude who brought the pigsticker over from Egypt. He's around here somewheres. Kinda a snotty guy, if ya pardon my French.
Can't help ya with that, toots.
Tell ya what, toots: you cook it for me first, and I'd be happy to oblige.
Hey, hang onto those. They could come in handy! I use my snips all the time!
Hey, that's the real pigsticker! Don't go pointin' it at me. Take it to the copper, girlie.
What's this, some kinda Eau de Snake? Don't get any of it on me; it stinks.
Whaddaya, lookin' for one wise guy? Har har!
No thanks. It sticks to the roof of my mouth.
No thanks, girlie. There ain't much market for big ol' bones.
Looks like one of them things the jockeys use.
I ain't takin' anything from YOU, lady. Why, that ankh could be stolen!
You keep it, lady. Maybe you can take some NOTES in it!
So it's a lightbulb. Whoop-dee-doo.
No thanks. I never look at nobody else's rap sheet. Professional courtesy, dontcha know.
No dice, lady. Get your own drink. It's an open bar; every man for himself.
It ain't mine, but I'll let ya in on a trade secret: there's a way to read what was typed on carbon paper.
Well, I ain't gonna tell ya exactly, or they'll throw me outta the Stoolie's Union. But it CAN be done!
Hey, you ain't supposed to be walkin' around with that thing. You're gonna spoil the barbecue.
